subject: Pilot runway gap — last-mile top-up vs short extension
messages:
From: Eli Navarro <eli@brightleaflabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Kate O'Connell <kate@brightleaflabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-28 09:12 -0700
Subject: Pilot runway — usage shortfall and options

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note — our pilot with Redwood runs out next Friday (Nov 6) and we just noticed the environment consumed ~82% of the allocated tokens after a last-week surge. We still have a few key validation jobs to run (NLP evaluation for search relevance) and procurement/legal timelines make a full contract by Nov 6 unlikely.

Two things we wanted to ask:
- Can we buy a one-time top-up (100k tokens) to complete the remaining tests and get to a meaningful evaluation?
- Alternatively, would Redwood consider a short 7-day extension to the pilot (no additional usage charge, or heavily discounted) so we can finish tests while procurement finalizes PO?

Attached is a small usage export and a screenshot of token burn by pipeline for your ops team to eyeball. If you need us to prioritize which tests to run and how much token headroom we need, Kate and I can provide details.

We need an answer today or tomorrow to feed procurement — if we don’t have runway we’ll have to pause tests and that likely pushes any expansion conversations into December.

Thanks — appreciate any quick guidance.

Best,
Eli Navarro
Head of ML, BrightLeaf Labs
eli@brightleaflabs.com

Attachments:
- usage_report_q4.csv (csv)
- screenshot_token_burn.png (png)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Eli Navarro <eli@brightleaflabs.com>
Cc: Kate O'Connell <kate@brightleaflabs.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway — usage shortfall and options

Hi Eli — thanks for the heads up and for sending the usage files. I pulled the CSV and the patterns look like the late-stage validation pipelines spiked (same as you described). A few quick, practical options we can execute today: 

Option A — One-time top-up
- 100,000 token additive credit applied to your pilot account immediately
- Cost: $1,200 (list rate) with a BrightLeaf partner discount of 15% -> $1,020
- Pros: immediate, no contract change; good if you only need a focused run
- Cons: can't extend the end date of access (tokens still expire at pilot end)

Option B — 7-day runway extension (short extension addendum)
- Extend pilot by 7 days to Nov 13; apply a usage cap or roll-forward for the extension window
- Pricing: standard approach would be charged at list, but we can offer a 60% discount on token units during the extension (effectively lower per-token cost) or offer a no-charge extension for critical finishing runs if procurement shares a PO intent email by Nov 9
- Pros: fixes calendar/ops issue and gives more buffer for procurement
- Cons: requires a short addendum and sign-off from our legal/finance team (can be done fast if you can get a procurement intent email)

If you confirm Option A I can bill and push the credit immediately. If you prefer Option B I need procurement to send a note (simple intent is fine) and I’ll loop in David to get the addendum executed.

Also tagging David Kim (cc) — David, can we greenlight a one-off 60% extension discount for BrightLeaf if they provide procurement intent? If not, what’s the fastest route for a no-cost, time-limited run?

Eli/Kate — which do you prefer? I can action either today.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 415-555-0199
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28 11:25 -0700
Subject: Internal — BrightLeaf extension/discount ask (urgent)

David / Marissa — quick summary: BrightLeaf (deal DL-2026-5587) hit ~82% token usage and needs runway for last validation steps. Customer asked for either a 100k token top-up (simple bill) or a 7-day extension (discount/no-charge). They can provide a procurement intent email by Nov 9 if that helps legal move fast.

Numbers: top-up revenue = $1,020 after AE discount (immediate). If we do 7-day extension at 60% off on token units, estimated gross delta vs list ~ -$2,400 for the extension window (depends on consumption).

Ask: can we approve a 60% extension discount conditioned on receiving a procurement intent email? If you prefer, we can bill the 100k top-up (clean, immediate) and treat the extension as a later addendum. Customer prefers to avoid invoices if possible because procurement cycles are tight.

Operational asks:
- Marissa: can you prepare the short addendum template (7 days, cap clause) so legal can sign ASAP if we go that route?
- David: confirm whether Finance can accept procurement intent as sufficient to proceed with a no-charge extension, and whether we should attach a PO requirement by Nov 20 as a fallback.

I’ll stand by and coordinate with Eli once you confirm. Time sensitive — they need an answer today/tomorrow.

Thanks,
Stephanie
From: Eli Navarro <eli@brightleaflabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Kate O'Connell <kate@brightleaflabs.com>
Date: 2026-10-31 17:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot runway — usage shortfall and options

Stephanie — thanks for the quick follow-up and for looping David. After a quick sync with procurement, we’ll take Option A (100k top-up) so we can finish the remaining validation runs without paperwork delay. Please send an invoice/charge and that will get routed today.

Also attaching our PO when it’s convenient — procurement asked that we include a formal PO reference on the invoice (attached here). We’ll schedule a 30-minute check-in next week to run through results and potential sizing for Dedicated.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Eli
Head of ML, BrightLeaf Labs
eli@brightleaflabs.com

Attachment:
- brightleaf_po_6789.pdf (pdf)
